打.meaning: The road crew has lost its hammer, so a retired sailor drags his old <part>anchor</part> down the <part>street</part> and swings it at every loose cobble. Clang! Clang! Each stone sinks flat with one <kanji>strike</kanji>.
打.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck waddles across the road just in time, and the anchor misses its tail by a feather.
打.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>f!' grunts the sailor with every swing, and the dust makes him sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

診.meaning: At the zoo clinic, a <part>speech</part> bubble pops up: 'Say aah!' A <part>person</part> in a white coat leans into the lion's mouth, counts its <part>whiskers</part> and listens to its heart. All healthy. That's the lion's yearly <kanji>checkup</kanji>.
診.on: The lion is fine, but it kicks the vet in the <sound>shin</sound> on the way out.
診.kun: Next in line is a nervous <sound>mee</sound>rkat, standing up tall to be looked over.

符.meaning: At the public bath, the attendant snaps off a little tag of <part>bamboo</part> and loops a string to <part>attach</part> it to your wrist. Lose it and you'll never see your clothes again. That clacking tag is your <kanji>token</kanji>.
符.on: You doze off on a <sound>fu</sound>ton in the rest room, and the bamboo token clacks on the floor.

色.meaning: A painter throws a <part>boomerang</part> dipped in paint around her bedroom. Each time it swoops back, it splashes the <part>bed</part> a new shade: red, blue, yellow, green. By dinner the quilt is a rainbow of <kanji>color</kanji>.
色.on: Then the wet boomerang clips a lamp, and the painter gets a nasty electric <sound>shock</sound>.
色.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals a striped <sound>ro</sound>dent, scurrying off the painted bed.

勘.meaning: A strongman whose arm <part>muscle</part> is <part>tremendously</part> big stops in front of a box he's meant to lift. Something feels wrong. He can't say why, so he walks away, and the box turns out to be full of bees. He trusts his <kanji>intuition</kanji>.
勘.on: Instead he lifts a single pink <sound>car</sound>nation, and feels much safer.

貴.meaning: A pearl diver guards one <part>shellfish</part>. Above it she lays <part>one</part> plank like a shelf, and on that a little box with a <part>mouth</part> for a lid, a <part>pole</part> pushed through it as a lock. Inside is the only pink pearl in the sea: <kanji>precious</kanji>.
貴.on: She wears the <sound>key</sound> to the lock on a string round her neck, even in the bath.
貴.kun: '<sound>Tut</sound>!' she clicks at a greedy gull, and hides the box on top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

銀.meaning: At the robot races, a clanking <part>robot</part> crosses the line one nose behind a racer covered in <part>gold</part> paint. No cup for second place, but the judge hangs a pale, shiny medal round its neck that is grey like moonlight. Second best is <kanji>silver</kanji>.
銀.on: 'Let's be<sound>gin</sound> again next year,' beeps the robot, and starts oiling its wheels.
銀.kun: It hides its medal behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld, a sleeping <sound>ro</sound>dent, a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic and a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t.

袋.meaning: You forgot your shopping bag, so you find a <part>substitute</part>: you pull off an old <part>garment</part>, knot the sleeves and fill it with apples. A shirt with a belly full of fruit. It works as a <kanji>sack</kanji>.
袋.on: For a handle, you knot your necktie round the top: now it's a sack with a <sound>tie</sound>.
袋.kun: Into the sack go a <sound>fu</sound>ton, a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock and a sleepy <sound>ro</sound>dent.

博.meaning: A <part>tennis player</part> loses <part>ten</part> matches in a row, so she quits and studies the game for years: spin, wind, strings. She writes a thousand-page book on the backhand. Now her name has a <kanji>Dr.</kanji> in front of it.
博.on: At her graduation party, she serves <sound>huck</sound>leberry pie off her racket.

預.meaning: Before your holiday, you plan <part>beforehand</part>: you carry your <part>rubber duck</part> to the bank, and a clerk locks it in the vault and hands you a ticket. It will be safe until you're back. You've made a <kanji>deposit</kanji>.
預.on: The clerk gives you a free pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt for opening an account.
預.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' says the clerk, sniffing the duck, 'it smells of yu<sound>zu</sound>,' and leaves it with the guard.

紛.meaning: A knitter is nearly done with a sweater when her cat grabs a loose <part>part</part> of the <part>thread</part> and runs. She chases it, drops her stitches, then forgets what she was knitting. One tug pulled her mind away: it's easy to <kanji>distract</kanji> her.
紛.on: Then a ty<sound>phoon</sound> blows in through the window and scatters the wool everywhere, and she forgets the cat too.
紛.kun: In the mess, a lla<sound>ma</sound> and two <sound>gee</sound>se slip in and hide among the wool balls: lost in the crowd.

釣.meaning: On a riverbank, an old man ties a <part>gold</part> coin to his line and hangs a <part>scoop</part> under it for a hook. The coin flashes in the water, and a greedy trout snaps at the shine. That's his secret for <kanji>angling</kanji>.
釣.on: Instead of a trout, he hauls up a mermaid's pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker, wrapped round the scoop.
釣.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes, and the line jerks: a bite!

感.meaning: A tough <part>drill sergeant</part> yells at his troops all day and never smiles. Then a puppy waddles across the yard, and his <part>heart</part> melts: his chin wobbles, his eyes fill up. Even he is full of <kanji>emotion</kanji>.
感.on: He sniffs, and tucks a pink <sound>car</sound>nation behind the puppy's ear.

障.meaning: In a relay race, a scout's <part>pennant</part> pole gets tangled in the <part>badge</part> sash of the kid in the next lane. They trip over each other, flags flapping, and nobody can move forward. Each one gets in the way to <kanji>hinder</kanji> the other.
障.on: The crowd laughs: it's the funniest <sound>show</sound> of the whole race day.
障.kun: Then a <sound>sa</sound>rdine sandwich falls from a picnic onto the track, and the next runner skids on it: '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

幹.meaning: In a forest café, the oldest oak has lost all its branches. Now the cook grills a <part>kebab</part> on one side of it, opens a sun <part>umbrella</part> on the other and nails a <part>drying rack</part> for tea towels to the bark. Only the <kanji>tree trunk</kanji> is left, holding up the whole café.
幹.on: A pink <sound>car</sound>nation grows out of a knot in the bark, the last flower on the old tree.
幹.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat climbs up the trunk and finds a hole with a rusty <sound>key</sound> inside.

世.meaning: In Grandpa's barn, three <part>pole</part> posts stand side by side, joined by <part>one</part> crossbar and a long floorboard. Each was planted the year someone was born: Grandpa's, Mum's, yours. Every post marks a <kanji>generation</kanji>.
世.on: A red <sound>se</sound>tter dog sniffs each post and wags at the newest one.
世.kun: On top of each post, someone has left a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt for whoever comes next.

葉.meaning: A family of ants has no camera, so for their <part>family photo</part> they climb a <part>tree</part> and stand in a row, with tufts of <part>grass</part> stuck on their heads for hats. Click! The picture is printed on the only paper they've got: a <kanji>leaf</kanji>.
葉.on: Then the ants ride back down the tree on a <sound>yo</sound>-yo, bobbing up and down and up.
葉.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the smallest ant, as the wind blows the leaf away, photo and all.

絡.meaning: Two climbing roses grow up a garden fence, and the gardener ties <part>each</part> one with green <part>thread</part>. By summer the stems have wound round and round each other so tightly you can't tell whose flower is whose. They <kanji>entwine</kanji>.
絡.on: A hiker leans his <sound>ruck</sound>sack on the fence, and by evening a rose has curled round its straps.
絡.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps from the pond and lands in the tangle of stems. '<sound>Rah</sound>!' it gurgles, stuck fast.

湯.meaning: You leave a bucket of <part>water drops</part> from last night's rain out on the balcony, and the <part>sunbeams</part> pour down on it all afternoon. By evening it steams. Dip a finger: ouch! It's <kanji>hot water</kanji>, ready for a bath.
湯.on: You test it with your big <sound>toe</sound> and yank it straight back out.
湯.kun: You drop in a sprig of <sound>eu</sound>calyptus, and the steam smells like a forest.

郵.meaning: On a lonely road, a tired mail carrier lets the <part>pennant</part> on her cart <part>droop</part>: no letters today. Then a sack of postcards drops from a passing plane, and up goes the flag. Everyone runs out: the <kanji>mail</kanji> is here!
郵.on: Up in the hills, the letters are delivered by a <sound>u</sound>nicorn with a satchel hung on its horn.

御.meaning: At a ski resort, the <part>chairlift</part> carries crates of potatoes bought <part>wholesale</part> up to a mountain hut, where a bellhop in white gloves bows to each crate and calls it 'sir'. Even the potatoes get a title here. Everything is <kanji>honorable</kanji>.
御.on: The bellhop wears ski <sound>go</sound>ggles while he bows, so his eyes don't fog up.
御.kun: '<sound>On</sound>ly the best for you, sir,' he murmurs to a sack of carrots.

奥.meaning: Behind a <part>slash</part> of curtain stands a <part>large</part> wooden <part>frame</part>, like a cupboard, stacked with sacks of <part>rice</part>. Squeeze past them, deeper and deeper, until the noise of the house fades away. You've reached the hidden <kanji>interior</kanji>.
奥.on: Right at the very back grows a tiny <sound>oa</sound>k tree in a pot that nobody ever waters.
奥.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' you gasp: in the dark, a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo has built its nest on the rice.

念.meaning: A puppy sits by the table, one paw pressed to its <part>heart</part>, staring at the sausage. Not later, not after dinner: <part>now</part>! It doesn't bark or beg, it just hopes with all its might. That's a <kanji>wish</kanji>.
念.on: The sausage rolls off the plate and lands on the crisp white li<sound>nen</sound> tablecloth, right by its nose.

残.meaning: After the feast, only <part>bones</part> lie on the plates, and the knights hang their forks on the <part>spear rack</part>. One sausage still sits alone in the pan. Everything else is gone: that's the <kanji>remainder</kanji>.
残.on: The cook scrapes the last cold corner of la<sound>sagn</sound>a out of the dish.
残.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' cries a hungry <sound>ko</sound>ala, too late for the feast, and licks the last plate clean.

暑.meaning: The <part>sun</part> hangs low and heavy over the beach, and <part>someone</part> in a straw hat lies flat on the sand, too sticky to move, fanning himself with a slice of watermelon. Even the air feels damp and thick. It's <kanji>sultry</kanji>.
暑.on: He crawls to the little beach <sound>sho</sound>p, but it has run out of ice.
暑.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>...' he sighs, and the heat makes him sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

豆.meaning: A cow with tiny <part>horns</part> balances a jar on her head, its <part>mouth</part> stuffed full and a lid on top. With every step, something small and round rattles inside and pops out: brown, green, speckled. The jar is full of <kanji>beans</kanji>.
豆.on: One bean pops out and lands right on the farmer's big <sound>toe</sound>.
豆.kun: A hungry lla<sound>ma</sound> snaps it up and trades it for a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.

頭.meaning: A <part>rubber duck</part> floats in the bath with a bowl of <part>beans</part> balanced on top of it like a hat. Every time it bobs, a bean rolls off. The bowl sits right where its brain should be: on its <kanji>head</kanji>.
頭.on: A bean rolls off the duck and plops onto your big <sound>toe</sound>.
頭.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' you laugh, and swap the bowl for a <sound>ta</sound>co, while your <sound>ma</sound>ma rolls her eyes.

喜.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> in a top hat wins the village prize and lifts his bowl of <part>beans</part> high over his head. His <part>mouth</part> opens in a huge cheer, and he dances a jig on the table. He's so happy he could burst. Hear him <kanji>rejoice</kanji>!
喜.on: The mayor hands him a golden <sound>key</sound> to the village.
喜.kun: He celebrates with a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt, while a <sound>ro</sound>dent and a <sound>ko</sound>ala dance beside him.

菓.meaning: A sweet-maker picks <part>fruit</part> from her orchard, boils it with sugar and leaves it to set on a bed of <part>grass</part> blades. Snap! It turns hard, shiny and sticky, red and orange. Kids queue round the block for her <kanji>candy</kanji>.
菓.on: Her bestseller is shaped like an orange <sound>ca</sound>rp, with a curly sugar tail.

震.meaning: A tiny <part>clam</part> is lying on the beach in the pouring <part>rain</part> when the ground starts to jolt and rumble. Its shell rattles, the sand jumps and the crabs scatter. The whole shore is shaking: it's a <kanji>quake</kanji>.
震.on: The clam bounces up and smacks a passing crab on the <sound>shin</sound>.
震.kun: A crab hides under a soggy <sound>fu</sound>ton, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> trembles in a doorway.
